conviction_note: The findings net to about zero (+0.1). The company's own July recurring run rate puts FQ1 revenue roughly at the $52-54M bar. Positive peer evidence (Allegion Americas non-residential low-double-digit organic growth in the same Jul-Sep quarter) is offset by the lapping of the April/July 2025 price increases and by component cost risk. Both numbers sit near zero, so the 1-2 point gap between them is not information.

findings.finding: Recurring service revenue (RSR) growth is decelerating, and the company's own numbers set FQ1. RSR grew +15.4% in FQ3 ($24.9M) and +12.9% in FQ4 ($25.3M, up only $0.4M sequentially). The FQ4 release's ~$103M prospective annual run rate based on July 2026 implies ~$8.6M a month, or ~$25.8M for FQ1, about +10% on the $23.4M a year ago. Management said the run rate rises 'to the back end of the year' as the 40%-higher FQ4 radio shipments activate with a 5-7 month lag.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock trades as a recurring-revenue compounder. FQ3 (2026-05-04): RSR +15.4% with a non-GAAP EPS beat, stock -15.2%. FQ4 (2026-08-24): RSR +12.9% with an EPS beat, stock -1.31%. A slowing RSR has not been rewarded.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The run rate is in the company's own release, and consensus revenue of $52-54M already embeds ~10% RSR. If the market had fully reset to a ~10% RSR grower, the stock would not have rallied 8% in 20 days into the print. Small residual: an RSR print near +10%, the slowest in several years, lands on the line this name is valued on.
findings.independence: Call transcript (Aug 24) on the 5-7 month activation lag and back-half reacceleration: https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262128672-tradingkey. Same company, different document. This lies inside what the company signalled, so the finding is sized toward 0.

findings.finding: Equipment pricing tailwind fades in FQ1 FY27. The FY26 10-K attributes ~6.1% of door-locking revenue growth and ~9.1% of intrusion/access-alarm growth to pricing. The increases were late April 2025 (tariff) and mid-July 2025 (annual), both fully lapped in Jul-Sep 2026. Equipment growth must now come from volume, led by radios, which carry ~20% hardware margin, against a prior-year equipment base of $25.7M (+12.3%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Equipment growth and margin were the swing line in Feb-2025 (-26.6%, distributor destocking) and Feb-2026 (+11.2%, better channel buying and margins). FQ4 equipment was +7.7% with radios pressuring equipment margin.
findings.why_not_priced: Pricing contribution sits in the 10-K MD&A, not in the release or the wire previews, and no preview frames FQ1 as the first quarter with no price help. If it were priced, consensus would show equipment growth at low single digits. The $52.1-54M revenue bar implies equipment of roughly $26-28M (+1% to +9%), a range that spans the question.
findings.independence: Timing of the April and July 2025 increases from a third-party FQ1 FY26 call summary: https://fintool.com/app/research/companies/NSSC/earnings/Q1%202026. Low radio margin and 'pricing actions are in place' (ambiguous on any new increase) from the FQ4 call: https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262128672-tradingkey. Net of the rest: RSR (~48% of revenue, ~90% gross margin) is roughly known at +10%, so this rests on the equipment half only. If an unannounced mid-2026 price increase exists, the finding shrinks to zero.

findings.finding: Peer read for NAPCO's locking business (Alarm Lock, Marks USA; K-12 and university). Allegion's Q3 2026 (quarter to 30 Sep 2026, released 2026-10-22, after NAPCO last spoke) showed Americas revenue +11.7% reported and +9.1% organic, non-residential organic growth in the low double digits from volume AND price, and a raised full-year organic outlook of 5-6%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Locking demand was cited as the driver of better equipment margin in FQ3 FY26 (stock -15.2% on the day for other reasons). On the FQ4 call management said K-12 and university demand were both strong and the project funnel was larger than in recent years.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. NSSC is +8% over 20 days, which may already include this read-through. NAPCO consensus figures on aggregators are stale (several still list August as the next date) and show no upward revision after Allegion. If it were fully priced, revenue estimates would have moved toward the upper $54M. This is a proxy, not a NAPCO number.
findings.independence: NAPCO's own FQ4 call: distributor 'inventory levels are good, sell-through is good' and no material change in early FQ1 demand (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262128672-tradingkey). Proxy: Allegion is mostly commercial mechanical, so the transmission to NAPCO's smaller locking line is not confirmed.

findings.finding: Component cost inflation risk to FQ1 equipment margin. Jefferies forecast memory pricing up 40-50% QoQ in 3Q26 on AI demand. On the FQ4 call (Aug 24) the CFO said data-center expansion is pressuring electronic-component costs, and the CEO said NAPCO had 'not been impacted at all as of yet' and was negotiating to hold agreed pricing and secure allocations.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross-margin quality has mattered. FQ4's 61.3% gross margin included ~600bps of tariff refunds, the beat was 'lower quality', and the stock fell 1.31%.
findings.source_date: 2026 (Jefferies 3Q26/4Q26 forecast; exact article date not confirmed from the URL)
findings.why_not_priced: Macro proxy. Nobody has quantified it for NAPCO, and management said it had no impact as of late August. If priced, gross-margin estimates would sit below FY26's ~55% underlying. Consensus EPS of $0.37-0.38 against $0.34 a year ago does not obviously embed a squeeze.
findings.independence: Company acknowledgement of the pressure on the FQ4 call: https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262128672-tradingkey. Macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by the company, so sized small.

findings.finding: Possible further IEEPA tariff refund in FQ1. The 10-K says the company had 'received or accrued certain' refund claims at 30 June 2026 and had submitted additional claims with no receivable recognised because collection could not be assured. CBP has processed refunds through CAPE since May 2026. Collection during Jul-Sep would add a non-recurring gross-margin and EPS lift, as in FQ4 (~600bps of gross margin, ~$0.09 EPS).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FQ4 carried ~$0.09 of refund EPS, beat $0.50 vs $0.41, and the stock fell 1.31%: the market looked through the refund.
findings.why_not_priced: The amount of unrecognised claims is undisclosed, and consensus of $0.37-0.38 shows no sign of a refund. A visibly priced refund would mean an EPS bar near $0.45. It has no path to guidance (none is given), so it is sized at a fraction of the same dollars as operating profit.
findings.independence: CBP CAPE refund processing since May 2026: https://www.gtlaw.com/en/insights/2026/5/us-tariff-update-section-122-duties-found-unauthorized-by-law-ieepa-refunds-under-way. Different source, but it does not show NAPCO received anything.

findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the Form 4 has been public for two months and the stock has since rallied 13%. Residual: an outgoing founder halving his stake right after a record quarter is an overhang and a signal that sell-side previews do not carry.
findings.independence: Donna Soloway's Form 4 (same days): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/69633/000141664626000002/0001416646-26-000002.txt. Same event, so counted once here.

findings.finding: Short interest stands at 2.48M shares (~7% of shares outstanding), 8.7 days to cover at the 2026-10-15 settlement, up from 2.35M / 6.6 days on 2026-09-30. On a stock averaging ~293k shares a day, a clean print forces slow covering.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb-2026 +11.2% on a good quarter is consistent with covering, but the cause is not established.
findings.why_not_priced: Days to cover is observable and therefore partly priced. It is a mechanism, not information: it amplifies whatever sign the print takes and adds a small upside skew to the reaction.

findings.finding: MVP cloud access-control (subscription, $3 per door per month) was guided on the FQ3 call to begin 'meaningful recurring revenue' around October 2026. On the FQ4 call the CEO hoped to report it around October-November, give or take a couple of months. The 2026-11-02 call is the first chance to give an update, and the 2026-10-21 release says NAPCO will showcase new recurring-revenue platforms at ISC East (Nov 3-5).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print has quantified MVP, so there is no reaction history on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: MVP is not in consensus RSR. Any first number or dealer count would be new; a further slip would be mildly negative, hence the range on both sides.
findings.independence: IR news list showing the 2026-10-21 ISC East release on recurring revenue platforms: https://investor.napcosecurity.com/news-releases.

findings.finding: Channel health going into FQ1: on the 2026-08-24 call the CEO said distributor 'inventory levels are good. Their sell-through is good' and that early-FQ1 demand showed no material change. FQ4 radio-unit sales rose 40% YoY and nearly 30% sequentially. A destocking repeat of the kind behind the Feb-2025 -26.6% looks less likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Destocking caused the Feb-2025 -26.6%. Recovered channel buying contributed to the Feb-2026 +11.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Company statement, public. Partly priced in a consensus that assumes growth. The residual is the low tail: a destock is less likely than the 16% implied move's width suggests.
findings.independence: Allegion's non-residential strength in the same quarter (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001579241/000157924126000032/exhibit991-pressreleasedat.htm). Shares a source document with findings 1 and 8 (the FQ4 call).

baseline_tension: The baseline has no usable skew and a thin, wide option market; the 8% 20-day run-up off near the 52-week low leans mildly optimistic. My findings net to roughly zero, so they neither confirm nor fight the run-up; the name's habit of selling beats moves p_up just under 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside what the company signalled): the RSR deceleration finding rests on the company's own July run rate, so it moved toward 0 (-0.5 to -0.3)
Rule 9 (net of the rest of the company): the price-lapping finding is on equipment only, with RSR roughly known, so it was trimmed (-0.7 to -0.6)
Rule 2 (one-offs): the possible further tariff refund was cut to a fraction (+0.3 to +0.2), since the FQ4 refund-boosted beat drew -1.3%
Rule 8 (understatement): abs_move_pct raised from 9 to 10, still below the indicative 16% implied move because the option market is very thin
Rule 1 (beats sold): p_up kept just under 50 (48 to 49 after the other caveats; net effect small)
Rule 6 (disputed revenue bar): all revenue-dependent findings were already capped small, so nothing changed
